newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - mixed, NYC sells out.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - mixed, NYC sells out.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were narrowly mixed in late trade on Wednesday, with the sale of the week, New York City's $1.072 billion offering, selling out even though prices were seen as rich compared to Treasuries.

The city started the day with about $515 million of tax-exempt bonds to sell to institutional investors, and by 1400 EST, had sold all but $50 million of the debt, which it awarded to its underwriters, who were led by Smith Barney, a city official said. Retail investors earlier placed over $304 million of orders during a presale period.
The city official added yields in four maturities were raised about one basis point, with some coupon adjustments, with the top yield in 2027 reset at 6.39 percent.
A trader, noting that the city's bonds looked expensive when measured against Treasury bonds, explained the new debt was competitively priced when compared with higher yield markets.
"I think they had a mixed bag on the long-end, they cheapened them up a bit and that surprised me," he said, explaining he had felt the deal was attractively priced.
Other sizable offerings that went to market included a $300 million sale of general obligation bonds by the Clark County School District, Nev., which fetched a true interest cost of 5.652 percent.
And the University of Connecticut's sale of $12 million of bonds was priced at 5.75 percent with a top yield of 2017.
The New York City Health and Hospitals Corp on Tuesday sold about $320 million of variable-rate debt, which will be remarketed weekly, at 3.6 percent.

An official with the corporation said it opted to sell variable rate debt because the yield was so low, and because it would be able to call bonds, if, for example, it entered deals with other companies to run the city's hospitals, causing some of the debt to become taxable, without premiums,
In the secondary market, prices were pegged at from up one-eighth of a point to down one-eighth of a point.

Traders said that the market failed to find much direction in part because Treasuries in late trade were assessed at around unchanged and while municipal futures ended stronger, they appeared to be playing catch-up.
Sikeston, Mo. electric revenue bonds of June 2022, which pay a five percent coupon, were bid at 5.87 percent, NET, down three basis points.
And North Carolina Medical Care Community revenue bonds for Wake County Hospital System of October 2026, which pay a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were offered at 5.90 percent, up one basis point.
In the futures markets, the June municipal futures contract was up nine ticks at 112-7/32. The June Treasury bond contract was down two ticks at 107-11/32. The MOB spread was 156 ticks.
